data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Genuine reliability is distinguished from mere compliance within a single evaluation by testing for structural coherence of errors across items: a genuine panel will exhibit correlated degradation on subtasks sharing an unlisted cognitive primitive, whereas mere checklist-tracking yields only independent, item-local errors.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the expert's intuitive errors also cluster by latent structure, the test cannot distinguish genuine reliability from expert-like competence.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the checklist is comprehensive and features independent, mere compliance may yield no errors and the test is uninformative.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If latent subtask structure is not recoverable from the evaluation items, the test cannot be computed.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If the checklist externalizes the cognitive operations constituting competence, the panel's errors reflect missing primitives and thus covary by latent subtask structure. Mere compliance produces errors only where the checklist under-specifies item features, which are independent across items.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
